summary: Takeshiro Kuraishi was a scholar of sinology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He held professorships at Kyoto University (~1939–1949) and the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958), and served as president of Chugokugo Gakkai (~1950–1974).

Takezo Kaneko was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1926–1929). He held posts at Hokkaido University (~1940–1947), the University of Tokyo as professor (~1947–1966), International Christian University (~1966–1976), and Seikei University (~1976–1980).

Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé. He succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche in 2012 and served as Supreme Head of the Nyingma tradition from around 2012 to 2015.

Taku Fukuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hajime Sakurabe. He was appointed lecturer at Doho University in 1995, and by 2026 was attested as professor there, part-time lecturer at Nagoya University, and affiliated with Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Takudo Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as a research fellow at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005–2006) and as a faculty member at Taisho University (attested 2015 and 2026).

Takushu Sugimoto, working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, earned his PhD at Tohoku University (1981). He was a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1990), Kanazawa University (attested 1993; professor emeritus ~2000), and Kinjo University (attested 2004).
Tamara Cohen works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto in 2023 under the doctoral supervision of Srilata Raman and Jürgen Hanneder.

Tampalawela Dhammaratana, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at the University of Kelaniya, the University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin (MPhil/PhD, ~1989–1994), and completed postdoctoral studies at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1994–1998).

Tan Chung is a historian and sinologist who earned a PhD at Visva-Bharati University. He held posts at the University of Delhi (~1964–1978) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994), and later served at Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.
Tan Poh Beng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam.
Tan Sitong was a Chinese scholar active in philosophy and Buddhist studies. During his career, he studied under Wang Zhengyi and later under Renshan Yang between approximately 1896 and 1897.

Tan Yun-shan was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Hunan Normal University, Chuanshan Academy, and other academies, he taught at Lida Academy and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University (~1937–1968).
Tanaya Afroz is a linguistics scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and held a post as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Tandin Dorji is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He has held appointments as a lecturer at the National Institute of Education, Paro, and as a history lecturer at Sherubtse College.

Tanero Sasakawa was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896). He held academic posts at Meiji University (~1921–1944) and Toyo University.

Tansen Sen is a scholar of history, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD under Victor H. Mair), and held a post at Baruch College (attested 2003).
Tanso Hirose was an 18th- and 19th-century scholar of sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801) and under Hōdō, going on to found Kangien in 1801.

Tanuja Ajotikar is an Indology and computational linguistics scholar. She has held posts at Harvard University, Maharishi Vedic University as Co-director of Sanskrit Department India Programs, and the Sanskrit Library as Assistant Professor (attested 2024–2025).

Tanzan Hara was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Shoheizaka Gakumonjo and Yushima Seido. He served in the Ministry of Religion (1872–1874), as Professor at the University of Tokyo (1879), and as superintendent at Komazawa University (1891).

Tao Jiang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo. He served as Associate Professor in the Department of Religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).
